Explain how photosynthesis works in plants.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs sunlight, which drives a series of reactions converting carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. This process is fundamental to nearly all life on Earth, as it forms the base of most food chains and produces the oxygen we breathe. The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes, while the Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
